subject: Geo-failover SLA exhibit and order-form language — clarifying credits & runbook
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Geo-failover SLA exhibit and order-form language — clarifying credits & runbook

Hi Sarah / MedTel team,

Following up from our call this morning — thank you for walking through your geo-failover requirements. Per the discussion, MedTel wants: regional latency SLOs (P95 per region), deterministic failover timelines for planned maintenance, and a higher-touch evidence/runbook attachment for cross-region restore.

I attached a first-pass "redwood-sla-exhibit-draft.docx" that tries to capture:
- P95 latency targets by region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and measurement windows
- A two-tier credit schedule that ties credits to % availability per calendar month with separate buckets for regional outage vs. global degradation
- A runbook appendix referencing on-call contact windows, escalation URIs, and DR playbook excerpts
- A clause on warm-standby capacity and estimated ramp windows for cross-region failover (30m warm, 4h full capacity)

Couple of asks for you so we can finalize order-form language:
1) Can you confirm the max allowable failover timeline for patient-facing flows (is 4 hours acceptable)?
2) Do you require a vendor-hosted evidence package (logs/trace URLs) or will a co-ordinated audit pull suffice?
3) Procurement: preferred redline workflow (DocuSign vs. consolidated PDF comments)?

If these are okay, David (Legal) will draft order-form wording and Monica (CS) will prepare the runbook excerpt to attach. Happy to jump on a quick 20-min review next week.

Thanks,

--
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Geo-failover SLA exhibit and order-form language — clarifying credits & runbook

Hi Olga — thanks for the doc. High level responses inline below and attached is a redline with procurement's top-level asks (MedTel_SLA_Comments.pdf).

Answers:
1) Patient-facing flows: 2 hours would be ideal for our primary region; for full capacity we can accept up to 6 hours for a full regional restore if mitigations are in place.
2) Evidence: procurement prefers vendor-hosted evidence (retained logs and signed snapshots) for auditability, but ops can accept a consolidated audit export if you can guarantee integrity.
3) Doc workflow: procurement prefers a single consolidated PDF with numbered comments, then DocuSign for the final signature.

Procurement notes (from their redline):
- Tighten the credit ladder to add an intermediate band for 99.5%-99.9% availability so we don't jump to full credits on a small degradation.
- Require an SOC2 control pointer for monitoring integrity of vendor-hosted evidence.

We can do a 30-min follow-up on Tue 1/19 10am PT if that works.

Sarah Liu
Sr. Manager, Cloud Ops
MedTel, Inc.
sarah.liu@medtel.com

Attachments: MedTel_SLA_Comments.pdf (12 KB)

Sarah / Olga —

Thanks for the feedback, Sarah. I attached a short plain-text snippet for insertion into the order form (orderform-proposed-language.txt) and annotated how Redwood can satisfy procurement's ask around vendor-hosted evidence while limiting scope:

- Evidence retention: Redwood will retain signed availability reports and diagnostic snapshots for 90 days by default, with an enterprise option to extend to 2 years (subject to costs).
- Integrity: evidence snapshots will be hashed and signed; we will provide an SOC2 control pointer for the monitoring and evidence generation process (fed into the exhibit).
- Credit ladder: proposed three bands (>=99.95, 99.5-99.95, <99.5) with proportional credits; added a carve-out for scheduled maintenance with a 72h advanced notice exception.
- Failover timeline: revised to allow for a 2-hour patient-facing RTO in primary region and a 6-hour full regional RTO; included an ops-led runbook appendix that Monica will supply.

Olga — once you review I can consolidate into the official exhibit and prepare a DocuSign envelope for the order-form + exhibit. Sarah — please confirm the 2-hour primary RTO acceptance so we can lock language.

Best,

David Kim
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

1) We propose adding a short pre-failover checklist (automated cache flush + prefix KV replay test) that can be triggered during a planned failover window; that lowers the full-capacity ramp from 6h to ~3.5h in most scenarios. Would you like that included as an optional clause?
2) DocuSign: Olga, David — if procurement is okay, I'll upload the final exhibit + order-form to the Drive folder and kick off DocuSign with MedTel after getting Sarah's confirmation on the 2-hour primary RTO and the intermediate credit band language.
